feed.title: WatchmanHQ: patch now
feed.subtitle: Flaws attackers are exploiting (CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog) in equipment small firms run, named in recent threat reports.
feed.rights: Published by WatchmanHQ (https://watchmanhq.com). Free, best effort, provided as is, with no warranty of any kind. Check the vendor's advisory before you change a device. CISA's catalog is public domain (CC0); these alerts are CC BY 4.0: credit WatchmanHQ.

entry.title: Exploited again: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (CVE-2026-0257)
entry.summary: Firewall or VPN (Palo Alto Networks). Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass security restrictions and establish an unauthorized VPN connection. CISA listed it as exploited on 2026-05-29, and it is used in ransomware attacks. Install the vendor's update, or its workaround until there is one, then follow the advisory's steps to look for signs of compromise: an update closes the hole, it does not remove an attacker who got in first. If the device gets no more updates (past its end of life), take it off the internet and replace it. Reported by: Group-IB, 2026-10-21; Unit 42, 2026-10-21; Unit 42, 2026-10-21; Unit 42, 2026-09-30; Recorded Future Insikt Group, 2026-08-07.

entry.title: Exploited again: BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS) and Privileged Remote Access (PRA) (CVE-2026-1731)
entry.summary: Remote support (BeyondTrust). BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS) and Privileged Remote Access (PRA) OS Command Injection Vulnerability. BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS) and Privileged Remote Access (PRA)contain an OS command injection vulnerability. Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute operating system commands in the context of the site user. Successful exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction and may lead to system compromise, including unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and service disruption. CISA listed it as exploited on 2026-02-13, and it is used in ransomware attacks. Install the vendor's update, or its workaround until there is one, then follow the advisory's steps to look for signs of compromise: an update closes the hole, it does not remove an attacker who got in first. If the device gets no more updates (past its end of life), take it off the internet and replace it. Reported by: Unit 42, 2026-10-21; Rapid7, 2026-10-19; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-16; Unit 42, 2026-09-30; Google Threat Intelligence / Mandiant, 2026-09-30 and 1 more.
